first.rationale:
Two of the three current problems are directly mechanical: onboarding completion -4% and activation -6%. memory_86 (shorter onboarding lifts completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (signup simplification lifts SMB activation) point at exactly that failure surface, and memory_91 suggests activation messaging is a complementary follow-on rather than a substitute, since messaging cannot rescue an account that never finishes onboarding. So simplify_onboarding is the single slot with the best claim on sustainable qualified revenue rather than borrowed revenue.

Verification choices: I pull memory_86 because it is the direct basis of my intended action, and consolidated summaries tend to shed the caveats that matter most here — specifically whether the completion lift held for paying/qualified cohorts or only for raw funnel counts, and whether the original test had a control holdout. I pull memory_73 not because I intend to price-cut but because competitor entry pricing is the strongest pull toward it this week; if its archived record shows the acquisition lift came with margin erosion, discounted-cohort churn, or a short measurement window, that closes off the tempting option cleanly. I deliberately do not verify memory_31 (redundant mechanism with 86, and its lift is only corroborating) or memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist is real but does not address either measured decline and is slow to read out in one week).

Downstream value risk: simplification can inflate activation and completion while degrading who arrives. Cutting required fields removes qualification signal, so the experiment must be scored on qualified revenue and 60–90 day retention of the new cohort, not on completion rate alone, with lead-quality and sales-acceptance as explicit guardrail metrics that can fail the test even if the headline number rises.

Uncertainty preserved: all six memories are consolidated summaries from days 12–61, and the day-76 environment now includes a competitor that did not exist in those tests, so prior effect sizes are directional, not predictive. Standard experiment scale with a real holdout rather than broad rollout — the evidence justifies a fair read, not a bet. If memory_86's archived record turns out to lack a control or to show quality dilution, I drop to a small guarded test and shift weight toward activation_messaging (memory_91), which touches accounts already past the qualification gate.
